posts.title: Fired for Speaking Up: Leadership After
posts.caption:
LEADERSHIP AFTER.

Getting fired does not end the leadership test. It starts a different one. A leader who loses the room has to decide what he carries next. He kept the ledger, he kept the receipts, and he kept showing up for the work. The next job is not revenge. It is building something that outlasts the room that cut you out. Document the decision, name the standard, and let the next room be one you built on purpose.

posts.title: Illegally Fired, episode 369: Thursday Check, Week Twenty-Seven.
posts.caption:
Illegally Fired, episode 369: Thursday Check, Week Twenty-Seven. Wednesday proved the mark, and Thursday files the proof. Twenty-seven weeks now, and every proved line gets filed where Friday can find it: the moving line files with its next step, dated and owned, and the waiting line files with its reason, written beside it in ink. A proof that stays on the desk helps nobody, so the file goes out today, stamped and sealed, and the week keeps its count where everyone can see it. The sealed lines stay sealed, the open lines keep their dates, and Thursday files the proof so Friday starts with the record, not the rumor. Twenty-seven weeks running, and Thursday files the proof. General information, not legal advice. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio. #CastleCalifornia #IllegallyFired #209 #KnowYourRights

posts.title: When a school district's budget goes sideways, the county office is the first line of oversight.
posts.caption:
When a school district's budget goes sideways, the county office is the first line of oversight. Every district budget gets reviewed by the county superintendent, and when the numbers do not add up, the state sends in FCMAT, the Fiscal Crisis and Management Assistance Team. They do not run the district. They read the books, name the gap, and hand the board a plan. Oversight is not punishment. It is the system checking its own math before the classroom pays for it. Know who watches the money, and you know where the power sits.

posts.title: One office holds more of your life on paper than any other in the county.
posts.caption:
One office holds more of your life on paper than any other in the county. The county clerk runs the elections, keeps the birth and marriage records, files the business names, and takes the papers you need stamped and kept. When you vote, the clerk counts it. When you marry, the clerk records it. When you open a business under a name, the clerk files it. The counter is public, the records are public, and the fees are posted, because the office works for everyone who walks in. Know what the clerk holds before you need it, and the trip takes five minutes instead of five weeks. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: Your water does not run itself.
posts.caption:
Your water does not run itself. In Merced County, your water comes from a district with a board, a budget, and a public meeting. The board sets the rates, approves the wells and the pipes, and answers for the water that reaches your tap. The meetings are public, the budget is public, and the minutes are public, because the district spends your money and delivers your water. When the rates rise or a well runs dry, that is a board decision made in the open. Find your district, read its next agenda, and ask what your water costs and why.
